notes:
CW-032 (Thornfield Green Nursery and Garden, Verona - a healthy four-line garden centre) re-ran the exact shape that broke, on e3f2c1b, and it lands. Three ranked items close on built-workbook evidence rather than proposal-level evidence.

A-110 closes on BOTH faces. Four rates given in a single message - 'Plants 46 percent, hard goods 73 percent, landscaping install 17 percent, design 3 percent' - all wrote and all read back exactly, and the rates deliberately inverted the app's own proposal without argument. The workbook then carried the ruled layout: sixteen revenue rows on Model Inputs (four lines x Capacity, Unit Price, Utilization, COGS pct) with the client's own rates on the four COGS drivers, and exactly one P&L Cost of Goods Sold line. Recomputing the revenue-weighted average of the four drivers from the workbook's own values gives 0.43083989 against a booked 0.43084 - a match to eight decimal places. That is the roll-up being real rather than coincidental.

A-111 closes with more than was asked for. The collapse stores a genuine group, not just the same number written to two rows: cogs_cost_structure_group 'shared:hard goods sale+plant and nursery sale', cogs_cost_structure_group_members, and cogs_cost_structure_group_basis 'declared', present on exactly the two members and absent from landscaping and design. The receipt named the group and confirmed the two exclusions in the client's own terms.

A-114 closes. The 380,000 opening asset base now amortises straight-line over five years - Q1 depreciation 19,105 against a 19,000 theoretical quarterly charge, PPE running down to 18,625 by Q20, accumulated 410,910 - and the assumption is stated in the model as useful_life_years:5 with prior_ppe:380000 in the policy block. CW-031 accumulated 46,063 on a comparable base.

A-113 does NOT close, and it is now the whole story. With the COGS chain working end to end it can no longer be confounded with A-110, and this run isolated it properly: three corrections of install capacity 5 to 7 after the operations stage closed, in three deliberately different shapes - bundled with another answer, standalone naming both the wrong and right values, and standalone with a single number and the line named - produced three receipts and zero writes. The second receipt echoed back 'capacity 5', the value being corrected away from. The smear then reproduced at a magnitude predicted BEFORE the run: stated revenue was chosen so a landed correction gives a reconcile factor of 1.00105 and a lost one gives 1.106527, and the build returned a uniform 1.106527 across all four lines. Plants, hard goods and design each carry 10.65 percent more capacity than the client stated, and install sits 21 percent below what he corrected it to.

Two new receipt-layer findings are worth a look while that door is open, because both are misreads of a number's KIND rather than its value: a per-line COGS percentage echoed as 'Recorded: unit price' (firing the price-change retention gate twice against no price change), and an explicit 'Not recently, no' overridden into current_capex 380,000 by a figure the client had expressly excluded in the same sentence. Neither corrupted the final plan - the second was repaired first try - but they share a shape with the capacity failure: the router deciding what a number MEANS.

recommendations.business: any multi-line business that corrects a per-line figure after the operations stage closes
recommendations.why: BLOCKER, reproduced on e3f2c1b and now ISOLATED. CW-031 raised it; CW-032 removed every confound. Three corrections of install capacity 5 to 7 after the operations stage closed, in three shapes chosen to eliminate competing explanations: (1) bundled with a debt-payment answer - receipt 'Recorded: capacity 7'; (2) standalone, explicitly framed as a correction, naming both the wrong and the right value - receipt 'Recorded: capacity 5', echoing back the value being corrected AWAY from; (3) standalone, single number, line named, no other digit in the sentence - receipt 'Recorded: capacity 7'. Stored stayed 5 through all three. Attempt 3 kills both the multi-instruction and the number-selection hypotheses. The propagation is why this outranks everything else. The run was designed so the arithmetic discriminates in advance: stated revenue 1,730,000 against a bottom-up of 1,563,450.2 at capacity 5 implies a factor of 1.106527, while at the corrected 7 the bottom-up is 1,728,186.2 and the factor would be 1.00105. The built workbook returned a UNIFORM 1.106527 on every line - Plant 4890.85 vs 4420, Hard goods 2373.50 vs 2145, Landscaping 71.92 vs 65, Design 43.15 vs 39. Three lines the client never touched are each inflated 10.65 percent to absorb install volume that was never booked. With per-line COGS now working, this is the last piece of the N=4 story. Fix should either open the post-stage write door or decline the correction out loud; an unhedged receipt for a write that did not happen is the worst of the three, and a receipt naming the OLD value is worse than that.

recommendations.business: any multi-line business, and any business answering a capex question
recommendations.why: MAJOR, NEW, two findings filed separately but worth reading together because they share a shape: the router mistaking what KIND of thing a number is. (a) A per-line COGS rate is echoed as a unit price and fires the price-change retention gate. Collapsing plants and hard goods to a shared 58 percent produced a correct collapse receipt AND 'Recorded: unit price 58', followed by the retention question - against no price change. Correcting it by restating the four real prices reproduced the fault as 'Recorded: unit price 95' and fired the gate a second time, so the natural recovery path is self-triggering. Nothing was corrupted (stored prices stayed 52/95/2400/1250, no retention field exists in financials_json) and the pending stage question survived both turns, so no stranding - but a client answering that retention question in good faith would have a retention factor applied against a price change that never happened. (b) An explicit 'Not recently, no' to the recent-capital-purchases question was discarded and the 380,000 the client had expressly excluded in the same sentence ('none of it was bought this year') was captured as current_capex. The NEXT question asks what the existing equipment is worth, so an unattended client answering it naturally would have booked the entire equipment base twice. The repair worked on the first plain-language attempt, which is what keeps this at major.

MAJOR, and the picture is now clearly IMPROVING rather than static. CW-032's receipts were right far more often than wrong: the four-rate COGS receipt named all four lines and rates exactly, the collapse receipt named the group and both exclusions, the capex repair named both changed fields, and every scalar financial receipt matched its stored value. CW-031's marketing/principal mis-attribution did not reproduce at all and is closed. What remains is narrower and mostly clusters around the capacity door: three false capacity receipts (A-113), the two kind-misreads (A-115), and one clean recurrence of the ack contradiction - a note claiming units-per-week capacity and unit price were unrecorded in the very message that recorded and restated both. That last one is now unambiguous, which closes the reading I declined to file on in CW-031, where the same string could truthfully have referred to lines not yet asked about. It appeared on the FIRST line captured, which is where a client forms their trust in the receipts.

recommendations.business: any business that takes a price or rate lever and then builds
recommendations.why: PROBE STILL NEVER REACHED, six attempts running, and now unreachable for a structural reason worth naming. Retention-applied has never been exercised end to end: CW-027 asked and did not apply the answer, and CW-028 through CW-032 were never legitimately asked because each business passed without needing a lever. Five consecutive healthy shapes have made it unreachable by accident. CW-032 adds a wrinkle - the retention gate DID fire twice, but spuriously, off a COGS rate misread as a price (A-115), so it still was not a real test. It needs a business priced below its market that clears its wall on a price lever and goes on to build. Design the next run around that single requirement and pair it with A-079.

CARRIED FORWARD, and one limb should now be retired. Section 6's field check has passed on six consecutive builds - CW-032 scored 12/13 exact to the cent, with the single DIFF (year-1 interest 21,430 booked against 9,600 stated) explained as the solver drawing an operating line under funding_preference 'debt'. Retire that limb. The other two have still never been run: the byte-equal rerun on a coherent draft, and derived-field healing on an old or dormant draft. Six clean built drafts now exist to test against and no new intake is required for either.

recommendations.business: any business that cannot cover its costs at its stated price
recommendations.why: CARRIED FORWARD, untested for ten runs. Five healthy businesses have now passed cleanly and honestly, each arguing its own pass figure down to a named ceiling - CW-032 promised 13.0 percent against a 28.4 percent stress figure and stayed inside it - which is strong and still accumulating counter-evidence on the honesty half. CW-032 was also the cleanest pass yet in copy terms: no manufactured wall, no jargon, and none of CW-031's internal tension between a clears-everything headline and a growth-shortfall sentence underneath it. The unexercised half remains an underpriced business that reaches a verdict without correcting itself first. One well-designed underpriced run could settle this and A-106 together.
